title: Threshold Setting
subtitle: Set a challenge that remains informative
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating threshold setting within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain threshold setting without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in threshold setting.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to threshold setting.

sections.explainSimply: The threshold determines when feedback is earned.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: A useful threshold is achievable enough to sustain learning but discriminating enough to represent the intended state. Threshold drift should be documented.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Manual and automatic thresholds influence reward rate differently. Report whether thresholds are fixed, adaptive, percentile-based or clinician-adjusted.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A rehabilitation plan: define the target, dose, measurement and stopping rule before changing the exercise.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand threshold setting to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Chasing a preferred reward percentage can hide lack of physiological learning.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using threshold setting predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Chasing a preferred reward percentage can hide lack of physiological learning. Evidence classification: implementation principle; limited comparative evidence.
